Install.metaTitle: Install in Claude Code, Codex & OpenCode
Install.title: Install TakoAPI in Claude Code, Codex & OpenCode
Install.description: One command installs the TakoAPI skill into your coding agent — discover and invoke AI agents through one unified gateway, and search the OpenClaw skills catalog. Works with Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode.
Install.stepUseAgentText: Ask your coding agent to find or call an AI agent on TakoAPI.
Install.heroSubtitle: Drop the TakoAPI skill into Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode — then discover and invoke any AI agent through one unified gateway, right from your terminal.
Install.whatWritesSkill: Writes a single, namespaced TakoAPI skill into each agent's own skills directory — it never edits your shared config files.
Install.whatTeachesAgent: Teaches your agent to call the <link>TakoAPI registry</link> and gateway over HTTP — no extra dependencies, no server to run.
Install.whatMcpServer: Prefer hosted tools? Register the TakoAPI MCP server instead — claude mcp add --transport http takoapi https://takoapi.com/mcp — exposing search_agents, get_agent, search_skills, and invoke_agent as native MCP tools.
Install.whatIdempotent: Is idempotent (safe to re-run) and fully reversible with <cmd>--uninstall</cmd>.
Install.whatApiKey: For the metered gateway, create an API key in your <link>dashboard</link> and export it as <cmd>TAKO_KEY</cmd>.
Install.footnote: On Windows or already in Node? Use <cmd>npx takoapi-install</cmd>. Prefer to read the script first? It's plain shell at <link>takoapi.com/install.sh</link>.

InstallTabs.universalNote: Installs the TakoAPI skill into Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode — auto-detected. Safe to re-run, no root. On Windows or in Node, use <npx></npx>.
InstallTabs.skillHeading: Skill — teaches your agent to call TakoAPI
InstallTabs.skillUniversalHint: …or use the universal command above — it covers {name} too.
InstallTabs.claudeCodeUse: Loads automatically — just ask Claude to find an agent on TakoAPI.
InstallTabs.codexUse: Invoke with $takoapi, or pick it from the /skills menu.
InstallTabs.mcpHeading: MCP server — hosted tools, nothing to install
InstallTabs.claudeCodeMcpHint: One command. Add --header "Authorization: Bearer $TAKO_KEY" to enable invoke_agent.
InstallTabs.uninstallNote: Removes only TakoAPI's own files — it never touches your other agent config.

Docs.title: TakoAPI API reference
Docs.description: Go from an API key to a working agent call: authentication, the discovery endpoints, the unified agent gateway, the hosted MCP server, error codes, rate limits and billing.
Docs.heroSubtitle: One key, every agent. Point any OpenAI-compatible client at TakoAPI and call an agent by its slug — or browse the whole catalog with no key at all.
Docs.quickstartIntro: Three steps from nothing to a reply. Every request on this page is a real call against the live API.
Docs.quickstartStep1: Sign in and create an API key in your <link>dashboard</link>. The secret is shown once, at creation.
Docs.quickstartStep2: Every example on this page reads the key from <cmd>TAKO_KEY</cmd>.
Docs.quickstartStep3: Set the model — or the slug in the URL — to any hosted agent from the <link>catalog</link>.
Docs.quickstartNote: The slug in these samples is a placeholder, not a real agent. Copy a real one from any agent page; only agents listed as hosted can be invoked.
Docs.authenticationIntro: Gateway calls are authenticated with a bearer token. The discovery endpoints are anonymous and need no key at all.
Docs.authHeaderNote: <cmd>x-api-key</cmd> is accepted as an alternative to the <cmd>Authorization</cmd> header. Keys always start with <cmd>tako_live_</cmd>.
Docs.authWhere: Create one key per client or environment in your <link>dashboard</link>, and revoke the ones you stop using.
Docs.authOnce: Only a SHA-256 hash of the key and a short display prefix are stored, so a lost secret cannot be recovered — create a replacement and revoke the old key.
Docs.authRevoke: Every call re-checks the key against the database and nothing is cached, so a revoked key is rejected on the very next request. Past usage stays in your history.
Docs.discoveryIntro: Four public, cacheable endpoints that need no key. Only approved agents and skills are ever returned.
Docs.endpointRegistrySummary: The whole agent catalog — Markdown for a model, JSON for code.
Docs.endpointRegistryNote: Without format=json the response is Markdown (text/markdown), split into a hosted-agents table and an open-source-projects table and sized to drop straight into a model's context — that is what the installed TakoAPI skill reads. Both formats are capped by limit, so check truncated and the total counts before assuming you have everything. Free-text parameters are truncated to 100 characters.
Docs.paramRegistryQ: Free-text match on agent name and description.
Docs.paramRegistryProtocol: Return only agents advertising this protocol.
Docs.paramRegistryKind: HOSTED agents are callable through the gateway; PROJECT entries are open-source repositories listed for discovery only.
Docs.paramRegistrySort: Ordering. Defaults to featured first, then most-called, then newest — and to most-starred for projects.
Docs.paramRegistryLimit: Total entries to return. Hosted agents are filled first, then projects.
Docs.endpointAgentDetailSummary: Full public detail for one agent, including its advertised A2A skills.
Docs.endpointAgentDetailNote: Only approved agents resolve; anything else is a 404. Moderation fields — review notes, internal ids and publisher avatars — are never part of this shape. Cached at the edge for 60 seconds.
Docs.paramAgentDetailSlug: Path segment. The agent's slug, as returned by the registry.
Docs.endpointSkillsDirectorySummary: The OpenClaw skills catalog, Markdown by default.
Docs.endpointSkillsDirectoryNote: Markdown-first like the registry. install is null for skills with no published install command — fall back to the github link. downloads is a third-party figure scraped from the skill's own listing, not a TakoAPI install count.
Docs.paramSkillsDirQ: Free-text match on skill name and description.
Docs.endpointSkillsSearchSummary: Full-text search across the skills catalog, JSON only.
Docs.endpointSkillsSearchNote: q is required: without it the endpoint returns an empty list rather than the whole catalog. Each result is the full catalog row minus readme and reviewNote; the example above is abridged.
Docs.paramSkillsSearchQ: Search term. Matches skill name, description and author.
Docs.gatewayIntro: Three ways to invoke the same agent. All three take a key, all three bill identically, and all three accept the agent's slug where a model name would normally go. Only agents of kind HOSTED can be called.
Docs.endpointChatCompletionsSummary: OpenAI-compatible. Point any OpenAI SDK at /v1 and set model to an agent slug.
Docs.endpointChatCompletionsNote: The whole conversation is forwarded: one A2A text part per turn, in order, with the OpenAI role attached to each part. usage is always present but always zero — nothing in this gateway counts tokens, and an agent need not be an LLM. Set stream: true for the SSE form above, and stream_options.include_usage to also get the trailing usage chunk. A non-streamed call times out after 30 seconds, a stream after 120.
Docs.endpointA2AMessageSummary: Native A2A passthrough. Returns the agent's own JSON-RPC response, unmodified.
Docs.endpointA2AMessageNote: Relayed as an A2A message/send call. Send the text shorthand, or a full A2A message — with parts, taskId and contextId — to continue a multi-turn task or pass file and data parts through. The agent's status code and body are relayed untouched, and a request with no content is rejected with a 400 rather than billed. Times out after 30 seconds.
Docs.endpointA2AStreamSummary: The same call over Server-Sent Events, for agents that stream.
Docs.endpointA2AStreamNote: Relays the agent's A2A message/stream frames verbatim as text/event-stream. This endpoint takes the text shorthand only. The connection is cut after 120 seconds, and the call is charged only once the stream reaches its end — see Rate limits and billing.
Docs.mcpIntro: TakoAPI runs a hosted, stateless Model Context Protocol server over Streamable HTTP at <cmd>{url}</cmd>. Register it once and your coding agent can search and invoke the catalog as native tools.
Docs.mcpAuthNote: The three read tools work anonymously. invoke_agent spends credit, so it needs your key: pass it as an Authorization header (Claude Code), as bearer_token_env_var (Codex), or in a headers block (OpenCode).
Docs.mcpToolsTableCaption: Tools exposed by the TakoAPI MCP server
Docs.mcpToolSearchAgents: Search the registry by keyword, category or protocol. Returns slugs, protocols and pricing.
Docs.mcpToolGetAgent: Everything known about one agent by slug — capabilities, protocols, endpoint, pricing and advertised skills.
Docs.mcpToolSearchSkills: Search the OpenClaw skills catalog. With no query it returns the curated top skills.
Docs.mcpToolInvokeAgent: Invoke an agent through the gateway and return its reply. Requires a key and spends credit.
Docs.mcpRateNote: The MCP endpoint is limited to 120 requests per minute per IP address, separately from your key's gateway allowance.
Docs.mcpInstallNote: Prefer a skill file to a server? The <link>installer</link> teaches Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode to call these endpoints over plain HTTP instead.
Docs.errorsIntro: Every gateway failure is JSON. These are the statuses the gateway itself returns.
Docs.errorsTableCaption: Error statuses returned by the gateway
Docs.error400When: The slug names an open-source project with no invokable endpoint, the request body failed validation, or every message turn was empty.
Docs.error401When: The key is missing, malformed, unknown or revoked.
Docs.error402When: The agent is priced and charging the call would take your balance below zero. Checked before the agent is contacted, so nothing is spent.
Docs.error404When: No approved agent has that slug.
Docs.error429When: The key went over its allowance in the last 60 seconds. Retry-After gives the seconds until the window resets.
Docs.error502When: The agent did not answer, timed out, returned no stream, or reported a JSON-RPC error over an HTTP 200. Never charged.
Docs.errorsOpenAiNote: On <cmd>/v1/chat/completions</cmd> the same failures arrive in OpenAI's envelope — with <cmd>type</cmd>, <cmd>param</cmd> and <cmd>code</cmd> always present — so an OpenAI SDK raises its usual exception types:
Docs.errorsPassthroughNote: A status the agent itself returned is relayed unchanged by the A2A <cmd>message</cmd> endpoint, so a 4xx there may be the agent's rather than ours.
Docs.limitsRate: The gateway allows 120 requests per 60 seconds per API key. The window is shared across every server instance and is keyed on the key itself rather than your IP address, so it neither loosens under load nor tightens behind a shared NAT.
Docs.limitsRateOverride: A key can carry its own allowance, which replaces the default for that key alone. Over the limit you get a <cmd>429</cmd> with a <cmd>Retry-After</cmd> header, in seconds.
Docs.limitsBillingFree: Agents priced FREE cost nothing — and so does any agent whose unit price is missing or zero. The gateway never invents a charge.
Docs.limitsBillingPriced: A priced agent debits your prepaid credit at its unit price, once per call. There is no token-level metering, so a call is one unit however long it runs.
Docs.limitsBillingPreflight: Your balance is checked before the agent is contacted. If the charge would take you below zero the call is refused with a 402 and the agent is never called — there is no overdraft.
Docs.limitsBillingFailures: Calls that fail are not charged. A 4xx or 5xx from the agent, a timeout, an unreachable endpoint or a JSON-RPC error all record the attempt and bill nothing.
Docs.limitsBillingStreams: Streams are charged only when they complete. A stream that is aborted, times out, fails mid-flight, or that you disconnect from early is recorded and not billed.
Docs.limitsBillingLedger: Every charge writes an immutable ledger entry against the invocation that caused it. Balance, ledger and per-call usage are all in your <link>dashboard</link>.
